prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1069; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On the afternoon of the reported incident in Baytown, Texas, I responded to a two-vehicle collision involving a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 1 was operating the first vehicle and Driver 2 the second. Driver 1 showed documentation identifying them as the named insured on the policy for the vehicle involved. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position of Driver 1's vehicle, and both Driver 1 and Passenger confirmed this at the scene. Driver 1 reported a knee injury and said the knee struck the dashboard during the impact. The injury description is consistent with the type and force of this collision. Damage to both vehicles is largely consistent with the impact described by the drivers, and photographs taken at the scene support several of these details. No independent witnesses were located. Neither driver reported, and I observed no sign of, prior damage to either vehicle. Both drivers were cooperative, and the vehicles were cleared from the roadway without further incident.
